ms.report:
Please find our submission for Milestone 2: Sourcing chips from manufacturers with required specifications.
We are excited to share that we have successfully sourced and tested NFC chips with EdDSA signing capabilities for our counterfeit-proof commerce solution.
Technical Implementation:
We have implemented a highly optimized EdDSA C implementation specifically tailored for the NXP LPC8N04 chip, which features:
・32-bit ARM Cortex®-M0+ microcontroller
・32 kB flash and 8 kB SRAM
・NFC/RFID ISO 14443 type A interface

The extremely compact form factor of the LPC8N04 makes it ideal for integration into product authentication solutions. In our demonstration video, you can see the tiny chip at the beginning where it's being pointed at, and we use the OM40002 development board (https://www.nxp.com/part/OM40002) to flash our C code to the LPC8N04. The final production solution will consist only of the LPC8N04 chip and an NFC antenna (which is already integrated into the OM40002 for testing purposes).
Technical Achievements:
Our implementation overcomes the significant power and memory constraints of the LPC8N04 through several innovative approaches:
・Optimized EdDSA Implementation: We optimized an already compact EdDSA implementation and tailored it specifically to work within the constraints of the LPC8N04's limited resources (which will be open-sourced in Milestone 3).
・Power Management Solution: Our TypeScript WebNFC implementation scans at specific intervals to maintain continuous power to the chip during cryptographic operations.
・State Machine with EEPROM Checkpointing: We developed a state machine that stores checkpoints of the EdDSA algorithm in the chip's EEPROM, allowing the chip to resume operations in case of power drops—a critical feature for reliable NFC-based authentication.

ms.promise:
Develop a proof of concept for chip programming by creating a working prototype that can sign any message using EdDSA when interacting with a phone.
Write code to integrate this process into a website, allowing the chip to sign a message, extract the public key from a successfully verified message, and resolve it to the entity that first registered it on-chain.
ms.criteria: The code for interacting with the chips will be open-sourced and should be easy to integrate into websites that can access mobile NFC features.
ms.report:
A. Output: Developed a proof of concept for chip programming by creating a working prototype using an NFC chip embedded in a physical garment that can sign any message using EdDSA when interacting with a phone via WebNFC.
Acceptance criteria: The code for interacting with the chips is open-sourced and easy to integrate into websites that can access mobile NFC features. The core library is published as an npm package for straightforward installation and integration.
Evidence:
・npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@uverify/asymmetric-nfc
・GitHub repository: https://github.com/UVerify-io/asymmetric-nfc

B. Output: Wrote code to integrate the NFC chip interaction process into a website, allowing the chip to sign a message, extract the public key from a successfully verified message, and resolve it to the entity that first registered it on-chain via Cardano.
Acceptance criteria: The Product Verification template provides a complete reference implementation demonstrating the full verification flow, from chip interaction to on-chain resolution, integrated into the UVerify web platform.
Evidence:
・UI template repository: https://github.com/UVerify-io/uverify-ui/tree/main/src/templates/ProductVerification
・On-chain transaction with product metadata and NFC chip public key: https://cexplorer.io/tx/44546e0ae1c1d8ec605b22daacea3f05cca4463c4d1bcdf4df41982256e9ca70?tab=content

C. Output: Produced a video screencast demonstrating the end-to-end process with the chips, including registering the public key on-chain, placing the chip in a demo product (garment of clothing), signing a random message, and verifying its signature and authenticity.
Acceptance criteria: The video demonstrates the complete flow from chip interaction through to on-chain verification, confirming the prototype functions as described.
Evidence:
・Video demonstration: https://drive.google.com/file/d/18rxccdpXN53ji9IWOmQ3ZlCEcoXyVyx0/view?usp=drive_link
・[NEW]Public key registration: https://drive.google.c
